gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Tightly packed display rows mark Oswald over Noto Sans Nushu below. And Noto Sans Nushu can drop a point, terminals held far out, a towering x-height still filling the column.
gen-cinzel-decorative-general-sans: Spaced capitals, a mild shimmer: Cinzel Decorative over General Sans. General Sans then glides at one pen pressure through copy, so a column never snags on a closed bowl.
gen-cinzel-decorative-work-sans: Mild crayon-on-paper shimmer in Cinzel Decorative over Work Sans, widely spaced capitals and stubby ascenders on the heading. One-width copy against that faint thick-thin is the lock.
gen-cinzel-decorative-satoshi: Refined display capitals over a soaring e: Cinzel Decorative with Satoshi. Satoshi holds a sans-serif one-width line, while Cinzel Decorative does that mild shimmer of weight best.
gen-boska-inter: Inter keeps a tube-like sans line, counters that breathe like a hollow reed, big counters under Boska. Boska does carved-stone stems best; Inter does that tube.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One comes through clean, lowercase nearly matching capitals, curves left unclosed. New Title wants a few huge words, letters locked like chain links, not a heading column.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps clean copy, capitals barely taller, counters connected outside. Noto Sans Saurashtra holds that sans line, while Oswald wants a few huge knit words, not a heading column.
gen-boska-gf-lexend-peta: Dramatic Boska carves stone stems with glass-scratch serifs over Lexend Peta. Lexend Peta walks a column of unthinned curves and wide-mouthed c shapes, so the run never pinches.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Dark lowercase stripe, curve endings never near: that is Noto Sans Sinhala. Tight Oswald rows over that dark stripe is the quality that holds the sans pair.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-plein: Drawn-string display, a couple of lines: Panchang over Plein. Plein can drop a point, a clear channel into every round letter still holding the sans-serif column.
gen-fs-panchang-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk keeps geometric copy, counters that breathe, a ribbon of constant width. And Panchang wants a few huge words, a brief burst of unsnagging string, not a heading column.
gen-fs-quicksand-roboto-slab: Contemporary Quicksand holds tube-like strokes, open mouths, short-looking capitals among large small letters over Roboto Slab. Roboto Slab can drop a point, slab-serif midzone still holding.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-hind: Quilon keeps an editorial ebb of thickness, large open counters in the rounds, a burst not a column, over Hind. Gentle swell against pipe-cleaner copy is the lock.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-quicksand: Quicksand keeps approachable copy, blown-glass bowls, identical bar thickness, terminals finishing far from stems. Quicksand holds that neon-tube line, while Quilon wants a few huge words, a brief editorial burst.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-abeezee: Marker-width daylight in every curve: Red Hat Display over ABeeZee. ABeeZee then walks a column of wide-eyed e letters, neon-tube thickness, so the run stays easy under that display line.
